item.title: HARRIS/McDANIEL: The Democratic Mayor Who’s Getting Black Men Right
item.description: Mayor Randall Woodfin of Birmingham is investing in the Black Male Initiative to provide concrete financial support and opportunities for Black men, which could help Democrats regain the support of this key voting bloc. The post HARRIS/McDANIEL: The Democratic Mayor Who’s Getting Black Men Right appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: GREENSPAN: D.C.’s School Mental Health System Works — Don’t Dismantle It
item.description: Mary's Center, a Federally Qualified Health Center, has provided school-based mental health services to 662 students in the D.C. area, and is urging the D.C. Department of Behavioral Health to reconsider their plan to phase out contracts with community-based organizations, as it would reduce their capacity to serve students and disrupt the continuity of care. The post GREENSPAN: D.C.’s School Mental Health System Works — Don’t Dismantle It appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: DEL’ROSARIO: What We Protect When We Vote
item.description: The residents of Washington, D.C., must be vigilant in exercising their right to self-governance and vote with an understanding of the potential consequences of their decisions, as Congress has the power to review and overturn local laws and budget decisions. The post DEL’ROSARIO: What We Protect When We Vote appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: EDITORIAL: Democracy is on the Ballot — Again
item.description: Voting is essential to defending democracy and ensuring accountability, dignity, and standards, as the cost of disengagement is too high for communities that have historically been marginalized. The post EDITORIAL: Democracy is on the Ballot — Again appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: EDITORIAL: When Black People Vote, We Honor the Sacrifices, Struggles, Commitment of Our Ancestors
item.description: As the midterm elections approach, it is important for citizens to exercise their right to vote in order to ensure that the future of Black rights, Black-owned businesses, Black equality, Black voting rights, and Black history are protected. The post EDITORIAL: When Black People Vote, We Honor the Sacrifices, Struggles, Commitment of Our Ancestors appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Things to Do, DMV: Weekend Rundown, March 5-8
item.description: From biblical epics to financial workshops, paint and sip nights to urban agriculture events, and a St. Patrick's Day parade to an International Women's Day celebration, there are a variety of events happening in the DMV this weekend! item.title: From Lament to Action: Baltimore Church Backs Racial Repair
item.description: The Presbyterian Church (U.S.A.) has launched the Reparative Justice Initiative, an ambitious plan to dismantle deep-seated bias and poverty in Baltimore, which includes allocating 15% of year-end non-committed funds to support Black churches and communities. The post From Lament to Action: Baltimore Church Backs Racial Repair appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: Henrietta Lacks Family Secures Settlement With Novartis Over HeLa Cells
item.description: The Lacks family has reached a confidential settlement with Novartis, resolving a lawsuit that accused the company of profiting from the use of Henrietta Lacks' cells without her knowledge. The post Henrietta Lacks Family Secures Settlement With Novartis Over HeLa Cells appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: D.C. Gas Prices Poised to Climb After Iran Strikes Shake Oil Markets
item.description: Gas prices in the D.C. area are currently about $3.10 per gallon, but are expected to rise due to U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran, which sent global oil prices higher and increased volatility in energy markets. The post D.C. Gas Prices Poised to Climb After Iran Strikes Shake Oil Markets appeared first on The Washington Informer.

item.title: District of Columbia Among Nation’s Top Places for Women, New Report Shows
item.description: The District of Columbia ranked second in the nation for women's economic and social well-being, health care, and safety, according to a new WalletHub report, with Massachusetts ranking first overall. The post District of Columbia Among Nation’s Top Places for Women, New Report Shows appeared first on The Washington Informer.
